name: Buffalo AKG Art Museum (Albright-Knox)
notes: The Buffalo AKG campus on Elmwood Avenue at the edge of Delaware Park. Refined 6 Oct 2026 from published descriptions and the ground file's OpenStreetMap outlines, not photographs (none reachable): the outlines show one long north-south range about 42 m wide and 135 m long with a round-cornered building apart at the north-west, so the campus was re-laid on them. E.B. Green's 1905 marble temple now stands at the north end of the range (about 42 by 47 m, cornice at 15 m, metal roof with the galleries' skylight), its Ionic portico and broad steps facing north to the drive, with porches on the east and west ends (the real ones are caryatid porches, the eastern overlooking Hoyt Lake); Bunshaft's 1962 Knox building runs south from it as the published 236 by 113 ft marble plinth (here 32 by 68 m, 7 m high, dark roof edge) round the court now roofed by Common Sky (the faceted glass canopy on its one spreading column), with the black glass auditorium box at its south-east; OMA's Gundlach Building (2023) at the north-west corner as a round fluted glass skirt with a marble top, joined to the old building by the glazed John J. Albright Bridge; the lake's tip at the north-east corner and the park's trees. Earlier model (24 Sep) had the Knox to the north and the temple facing Elmwood; on its outlines it stood 57% on them, now 90%. Still guessed: which way the 1905 portico faces (north is inferred from the outlines' narrow northern projection and the Knox to the south), the column count, the auditorium's place, the Gundlach's height and the bridge's route.
